questions.text:
If an object is having same weight at same distance above and below the surface of earth, find its distance from surface of earth.
(1) $\frac{R}{2}$
(2) $(\sqrt{5}-1) \frac{R}{2}$
(3) $(\sqrt{3}-1) \frac{R}{2}$
(4) $(\sqrt{5}-1) R$
Answer (2)
sol. $\frac{G M m}{(R+x)^{2}}=\frac{G M m(R-x)}{R^{3}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow R^{3}=(R+x)^{2}(R-x) \\
\Rightarrow R^{3}=\left(R^{2}-x^{2}\right)(R+x) \\
\Rightarrow x^{2}+R x-R^{2}=0 \\
\therefore x=\frac{-R \pm \sqrt{R+4 R^{2}}}{2} \\
x=\frac{(\sqrt{5}-1)}{2} R
\end{array}$$

de-Broglie wavelength of a proton and an electron is same. The ratio of kinetic energy of electron to that of proton is

questions.text:
If ratio of centripetal acceleration of two particles moving on the same path is 3 : 4. Find the ratio of their tangential velocities.
(1) $2: \sqrt{3}$
(2) $\sqrt{3}: 2$
(3) $\sqrt{3}: 1$
(4) $\sqrt{2}: 1$
Answer (2)

steps:
$a_{c}=\frac{v^{2}}{r}, \frac{\left(a_{c}\right)_{1}}{\left(a_{c}\right)_{2}}=\left(\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}}\right)^{2}$
$$\frac{3}{4}=\left(\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}}\right)^{2} \rightarrow \frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}}=\sqrt{3}: 2$$

If a biconvex lens of material of refractive index 1.5 has focal length 20 cm in air, then its focal length when it is submerged in a medium of refractive index 1.6 is
(1) -160 cm
(2) 160 cm
(3) 1.6 cm
(4) - 16 cm
Answer (1)

steps:
$\frac{1}{20}=(1.5-1)\left(\frac{2}{R}\right)$
$$\begin{aligned}
R & =20 \mathrm{~cm} \\
\frac{1}{f^{\prime}} & =\left(\frac{1.5}{1.6}-1\right)\left(\frac{2}{R}\right) \\
& =\frac{-1}{16} \times \frac{2}{20} \\
f^{\prime} & =-160 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}$$

questions.text:
Consider a series of steps as shown. A ball is thrown from $O$. Find the minimum speed of directly jump to $5^{\text {th }}$ step.
(1) $5(\sqrt{2}+1) \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$
(2) $5 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(3) $5 \sqrt{\sqrt{2}+1} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(4) $6 \sqrt{\sqrt{3}+1} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
Answer (3)

steps:
$y=x \tan \theta-\frac{g x^{2}}{2 v^{2} \cos ^{2} \theta}$
(2.5, 2.5) must lie on this
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow 1=\tan \theta-\frac{g \times 2.5}{2 v^{2} \cos ^{2} \theta} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{25}{2 v^{2} \cos ^{2} \theta}=\tan \theta-1 \\
\Rightarrow v^{2}=\frac{25}{2}\left\{\frac{1+\tan ^{2} \theta}{\tan \theta-1}\right\} \\
\Rightarrow v_{\min }=5 \sqrt{\sqrt{2}+1}
\end{array}$$
[Happens when $\tan \theta=\sqrt{2}+1$ ]

questions.text:
An electron is moving with speed of 1 m/s at distance of 1 m from a large sheet of charge with density $\sigma \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$. Find maximum value of $\sigma$ such that electron hit the sheet after 1 sec.
(mass of electron $9 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$, permittivity of free space $\varepsilon_{0}=9 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{C}^{2} / \mathrm{Nm}^{2}$ )
(1) $4.05 \times 10^{-22} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$
(2) $8.10 \times 10^{-22} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$
(3) $4.05 \times 10^{24} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$
(4) $2.02 \times 10^{-20} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$
Answer (1)

steps:
For maximum value of $\sigma$, initially, electron must move away from plate.
$$\begin{array}{l}
u t+\frac{1}{2} a t^{2}=s \\
t=1 \quad u=1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \quad s=-1 \mathrm{~m} \\
1 \times 1-\frac{1}{2} a \times 1^{2}=-1 \\
\Rightarrow \quad a=4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \\
\quad \frac{q E}{m}=4 \\
\quad \frac{q \sigma}{2 \varepsilon_{0} m}=4
\end{array}$$
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma & =\frac{4 \times 2 \times 9 \times 10^{-12} \times 9 \times 10^{-31}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \\
& =\frac{8 \times 81}{1.6} \times 10^{-24} \\
& =4.05 \times 10^{-22} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^{2}
\end{aligned}$$

Answer (3)

steps:
$\left|\Delta E_{0}\right|=\left(-13.6\left\{1-\frac{1}{4}\right\}\right)$ ev
$$\begin{array}{l}

\downarrow \longleftrightarrow \\
\lambda=\frac{12400}{10.2} \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~m} \\
\rho=\frac{h}{\lambda}=\frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 10.2}{12400 \times 10^{-10}} \\

questions.text:
In a convex mirror having radius of curvature 30 cm the height of image is half the object height. What will be the object (in cm ) distance?
Answer (15)

steps:
$f=15$
$$\begin{array}{l}
m=-\frac{v}{u}=+\frac{1}{2} \\
v=-\frac{u}{2} \\
\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f} \\
\frac{2}{-u}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f} \\
u=-f=-15 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{array}$$
